t: Under the amended Section 145, 'property' includes:
o: Only immovable property belonging to the Government
The insured vehicle itself and its accessories
Only goods carried in the insured vehicle
Roads, bridges, culverts, causeways, trees, posts, milestones and baggage of passengers and goods carried in any motor vehicle
e: The amended definition of property (s.145(g)) adds 'baggage of passengers and goods carried in any motor vehicle' to roads, bridges, culverts, causeways, trees, posts and milestones.

t: Besides the Act policy under Chapter XI, a vehicle carrying or meant to carry dangerous or hazardous goods must also have a policy under:
e: Section 146(1) proviso requires vehicles carrying dangerous or hazardous goods to also hold a policy under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991.

t: Motor Accident Claims Tribunals under Section 165 are constituted by:
o: The High Court of the State
e: Section 165 empowers a State Government to constitute one or more Claims Tribunals for specified areas to adjudicate claims arising out of motor accidents.

t: Under the amended Act, schemes for interim relief to claimants and for recovery of such amounts from the owner are provided by:
e: Sections 140–144 (interim no-fault relief of ₹50,000/₹25,000) were deleted; s.164A enables Central Government schemes for interim relief and recovery from the owner, with the Fund under s.164B.

t: Under the detailed accident report scheme, the Interim Accident Report (Form V) is to be submitted by the Investigating Officer to the Claims Tribunal within:
e: Timelines: FAR 48 hours, Form II 10 days, driver/owner forms 30 days, IAR 50 days, victim forms 60 days, DAR 90 days, insurer's Form XI 30 days thereafter.

t: Where the insurer contests liability in Form XI, the Claims Tribunal must complete its inquiry within:
e: Consent award – six months; quantum dispute after admission of liability – nine months; contested inquiry – twelve months from the accident.

t: A motor vehicle with seating capacity between 6+1 and 12+1 used for carrying passengers for hire or reward is classified as a:
e: Motor cab: up to 6+1 for hire/reward; maxi cab: more than 6+1 but up to 12+1 for hire/reward; omnibus: any passenger vehicle with capacity above 6+1.

t: The 2019 amendment substituted the term 'invalid carriage' with:
e: The amended s.2 uses 'adapted vehicle' for a vehicle designed/adapted for use by a person with disability; 'community service' (s.2(4A)) and 'golden hour' (s.2(12A)) were also inserted.

t: Under Section 129, the requirement to wear protective headgear while driving or riding a two-wheeler does not apply to:
o: A person riding within city limits
A person holding a learner's licence
e: Section 129 requires every person driving or riding a two-wheeler, other than a Sikh wearing a turban, to wear protective headgear conforming to BIS standards.

t: After the 2019 amendment, a non-transport driving licence issued to a person aged 30 to 50 years is valid for:
e: Amended s.14: below 30 – valid till age 40; 30 to below 50 – 10 years; 50 to below 55 – till age 60; 55 and above – 5 years.

t: Under Section 164 of the amended MV Act, the fixed no-fault compensation payable for grievous hurt is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 164 fixes ₹5 lakh for death and ₹2.5 lakh for grievous hurt, payable without proof of negligence. Nothing is payable under s.164 for minor injury.

t: Causing grievous hurt by an act endangering life or personal safety (old Section 338 IPC) now falls under:
e: Section 337 IPC (hurt) → s.125(a) BNS; Section 338 IPC (grievous hurt) → s.125(b) BNS.

t: The Mukund Dewangan case (3 July 2017) was decided by:
o: A Constitution Bench of five judges
e: The three-judge Bench held that an LMV licence covers transport vehicles of GVW up to 7,500 kg; the view was later affirmed by a Constitution Bench in Rambha Devi (2024).

t: The highest multiplier (18) under the Sarla Verma table approved in Pranay Sethi applies to deceased persons aged:
e: The operative multiplier of 18 covers the age groups 15–20 and 21–25; it reduces by one for every five years thereafter up to age 50.

t: A new feature introduced by Pranay Sethi over Sarla Verma was the grant of future prospects to deceased persons aged above 50 years at:
o: 15% for salaried on permanent job and 10% for self-employed
e: Sarla Verma gave nil for above 50; Pranay Sethi added 15% (permanent job) and 10% (self-employed/fixed salary) for the above-50 band.

t: Pranay Sethi directed that the conventional-head amounts be enhanced by:
e: The Constitution Bench fixed ₹15,000/₹40,000/₹15,000 with an increase of 10% in a span of three years to account for inflation.

t: Which head of compensation awarded in Rajesh v. Rajbir Singh was removed by Pranay Sethi?
o: Loss of care and guidance for minor children
e: Pranay Sethi disapproved the separate head of loss of care and guidance for minor children granted in Rajesh v. Rajbir, retaining estate, consortium and funeral expenses.

t: An appeal against an order of the Commissioner under the Employees' Compensation Act must be filed within:
e: The limitation table: EC appeal 60 days; MCOP appeal 90 days from receipt of the award; consumer appeal 30 days.

t: Under Section 177 of the amended MV Act, the general penalty for a first offence where no specific penalty is provided is a fine of:
e: The 2019 amendment raised the general penalty under s.177 from ₹100 to ₹500 for a first offence and ₹1,500 for subsequent offences.

t: After the 2019 amendment, an application for compensation under Section 166 must be made within:
o: Six months of the occurrence of the accident
Ninety days of the occurrence of the accident
Twelve months of the occurrence of the accident
Two years of the occurrence of the accident
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The amended s.166(3) reintroduced a limitation of six months from the accident; under the pre-amendment law there was no time limit for filing a claim petition.

t: A 7-seater maxi cab carries 11 passengers when it meets with an accident injuring all of them. The insurer's statutory liability under the Act policy extends to:
o: Only the passengers who had paid the fare
Passengers up to the registered carrying capacity only; persons beyond the seating capacity are excluded
None of the passengers, as the vehicle was overloaded
e: Passengers of a transport vehicle are third parties up to the registered carrying capacity; persons beyond the seating capacity are among the exemptions from liability.

t: During a Lok Adalat the presiding members propose a compromise figure for a death claim. Which statement about the forum is correct?
o: The Lok Adalat has the powers of a civil court under the CPC and its proceedings are deemed judicial proceedings
The Lok Adalat can impose a settlement even if one party dissents
A Lok Adalat award can be appealed to the District Court
Lok Adalat awards are mere recommendations with no binding force
e: Under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, a Lok Adalat has civil-court powers, its proceedings are judicial proceedings and its consent award is final and binding.

t: The designated officer offers ₹18 lakh; the claimant accepts before the Tribunal. What is the status of the claim?
o: It remains pending until the insurer files a written statement
The Tribunal must still conduct a full inquiry on negligence
It is deemed settled by consent and the Tribunal records the settlement
The claimant must file a fresh petition under Section 166
e: Under s.149(3)(a), on acceptance of the offer the Tribunal records the settlement and the claim is deemed settled by consent; payment follows within 30 days.

t: A private car owner was found to have concealed, at proposal stage, that the vehicle was used as a taxi. The insurer repudiates the TP claim. Which ground under Section 150(2) is invoked?
o: The policy is void for non-disclosure of a material fact / false representation
Use for a purpose not allowed by the permit
e: Section 150(2)(b) permits the insurer to avoid liability where the policy is void on the ground of non-disclosure of a material fact or a false material representation.

t: Under Pranay Sethi, for a deceased below 40 years holding a permanent job, the addition for future prospects is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Salaried persons on a permanent job get 50% (below 40), 30% (40–50) and 15% (above 50). Self-employed or fixed-salary persons get 40%, 25% and 10% respectively.

t: The driver of an insured bus is found to have 60 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood when he causes a fatal accident. Under the amended Act the insurer:
o: Can avoid liability only if alcohol exceeded 100 mg per 100 ml
Must pay without any right of recovery
Has no defence, since drunken driving is only a criminal offence
Can plead driving under the influence of alcohol under Section 185 as a specified defence under Section 150(2)
e: The 2019 amendment added breach of the condition against driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs (s.185, limit 30 mg/100 ml) as a defence available to the insurer.

t: A car with a package policy is sold on 1 March; the buyer does not inform the insurer. On 20 March the car injures a pedestrian. The TP claim:
o: Is not payable, as the policy stands in the seller's name
Is payable, since the certificate of insurance and policy are deemed transferred with the vehicle for third party purposes
Is payable only if the buyer applied within 14 days
e: Section 157 deems the certificate and TP policy to be transferred to the transferee from the date of transfer; the 14-day application concerns updating particulars, and court rulings require separate steps only for the own-damage part.

t: The police officer investigating a fatal accident has not forwarded any report to the Tribunal four months after the accident. Under the amended Section 159 this is:
o: Permissible, as the report is required only within thirty days of charge sheet
A default – the accident information report must be submitted within three months
Permissible, as there is no time limit for police reports
Permissible, since the report goes only to the insurer
e: Section 159 fixes a three-month period for the police to prepare and submit the accident information report to the Claims Tribunal and other prescribed agency.

t: Which of the following situations qualifies as a 'hit and run motor accident' under Section 161?
o: The driver is identified but absconds after the accident
The vehicle is identified but the owner disputes negligence
The vehicle is identified but was uninsured
A vehicle hits a pedestrian and the vehicle's identity cannot be ascertained despite reasonable efforts
e: The definition hinges on the identity of the vehicle being unascertainable despite reasonable efforts; where the vehicle is known, the ordinary s.164/s.166 remedies against owner/insurer apply.

t: Which statement about Section 164 compensation is correct?
o: The claimant need not prove wrongful act or neglect, and the amount is fixed irrespective of the victim's income
It is an interim payment to be adjusted in a Section 166 award
The claimant must prove negligence but the quantum is fixed
The amount depends on the victim's income and age using the Second Schedule
e: Section 164 is a fixed, no-fault, final compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt) independent of income or negligence, unlike the deleted s.163A structured formula and s.140 interim relief.

t: An insurer wishes to appeal an award of ₹8,00,000 passed on 10 January. By which date must the appeal be filed and what deposit is required?
o: Within 90 days of the award, depositing ₹25,000
Within 30 days of the award, depositing ₹4,00,000
Within 90 days of the award, depositing ₹4,00,000
Within 60 days of the award, with no deposit
e: Section 173: appeal to the High Court within ninety days; deposit of ₹25,000 or 50% of the award, whichever is less (50% = 4,00,000, so ₹25,000).

t: Which of the following persons would NOT qualify as a 'Good Samaritan' under Section 134A?
o: A motorist who in good faith carries the victim to the nearest hospital
A private ambulance operator who transports the victim for a fee
A shopkeeper who calls the police and stays with the victim till help arrives
A passer-by who gives first aid to the victim without expecting any reward
e: A Good Samaritan is one who in good faith, voluntarily and without expectation of reward renders emergency care or transports the victim; a paid service provider does not fit the definition.

t: Which of the following transport vehicles requires a permit under Section 66?
o: An empty vehicle with temporary registration proceeding for registration
An ambulance used solely for that purpose
A private taxi operator's motor cab plying for hire
A vehicle used solely for conveyance of corpses with mourners
e: Section 66(3) exempts ambulances, hearses, vehicles proceeding for registration or repair, goods vehicles up to 3,000 kg GVW etc.; a motor cab plying for hire needs a contract carriage permit.

t: Since 1 April 2021, the standard fire policy for a dwelling in India is:
o: Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bharat Griha Raksha for homes; Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha (up to ₹5 crore) and Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha (₹5–50 crore) for enterprises.

t: A bus operator wants a permit for carrying pilgrims for a festival lasting three weeks. The appropriate authorisation under Section 87 is:
o: No permit, since the use is non-commercial
A temporary permit, which can be granted for a maximum of four months
A regular permit valid for five years
e: Temporary permits under s.87 are granted for temporary needs such as conveyance of persons on special occasions, for a period not exceeding four months.

topic: Judgements – Pranay Sethi vs Sarla Verma
t: In a Section 166 death claim, the Tribunal should take the multiplier from one judgement and the deductions/future prospects/conventional heads from another. The correct pairing is:
o: Everything as per Sarla Verma, which supersedes Pranay Sethi
Whichever judgement yields the higher compensation
Multiplier as per Sarla Verma (Column 4 table); personal expenses, future prospects and conventional heads as standardised in Pranay Sethi
Multiplier as per Pranay Sethi; deductions as per Second Schedule
e: Pranay Sethi retained the Sarla Verma multiplier table (Column 4) and standardised future prospects (extending them to self-employed), personal-expense deductions and conventional heads.

t: A 'transport vehicle' endorsement is needed on a driving licence for which of the following?
o: A motor cab of ULW 1,400 kg
A goods carriage of GVW 7,200 kg
A goods carriage of GVW 9,000 kg
e: Per Mukund Dewangan, 'transport vehicle' for licensing purposes means medium and heavy goods/passenger vehicles above 7,500 kg; LMV-class transport vehicles can be driven on an LMV licence.

t: Who is eligible for cashless treatment under the Cashless Treatment of Road Accident Victims Scheme, 2025?
o: Any person injured in an accident caused by a motor vehicle, on any road
Only victims of accidents involving insured vehicles
Only victims holding a valid health insurance policy
e: The Scheme covers any person injured in a motor vehicle accident, with treatment at designated hospitals up to ₹1.5 lakh for seven days, funded through the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund.

t: A 16-year-old drives his father's car and injures a pedestrian. Under the amended Act, for the offence committed by the juvenile:
o: No offence arises, since the juvenile cannot hold a licence
Only the juvenile is punishable under the Juvenile Justice Act
The guardian or owner of the vehicle is deemed guilty and punishable, and the vehicle's registration may be cancelled for 12 months
The insurer is penalised for insuring the vehicle
e: Section 199A (2019) makes the guardian/owner liable (fine ₹25,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years) unless they prove lack of knowledge or due diligence; registration is cancelled for 12 months and the juvenile cannot get a licence till 25.

t: A bachelor aged 29, self-employed, earning ₹20,000 per month, dies in an accident. He supported his parents and a younger sister. Loss of dependency is:
e: 2,40,000 + 40% (self-employed, below 40) = 3,36,000; bachelor with parents and dependent sibling → deduct 1/3 = 2,24,000; × multiplier 17 (26–30) = ₹38,08,000.

t: A 63-year-old permanent employee earning ₹30,000 per month dies in 2025, leaving a wife and an unmarried daughter. Total compensation including conventional heads (+20%) is:

A 30-year-old self-employed mason earning ₹20,000 per month suffers 40% permanent disability, assessed by the Tribunal as 40% loss of earning capacity. Compensation for loss of future earnings (no future prospects added) is:
e: Injury cases: annual income 2,40,000 × 40% functional disability = 96,000 × multiplier 17 (age 26–30) = ₹16,32,000; no deduction for personal expenses is made in injury claims.

t: A permanent employee aged 44 earning ₹40,000 per month dies, leaving wife and one child. The annual multiplicand (after future prospects and personal-expense deduction) is:
e: 4,80,000 + 30% = 6,24,000; less 1/3 for 2 dependants = ₹4,16,000 per annum, to be multiplied by 14.

t: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act 1938, a life insurance policy cannot be called in question on any ground after how many years from the date of issue, revival or rider addition, whichever is later?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The 2015 amendment made the three-year bar absolute: after three years no policy may be questioned on any ground, including fraud.

t: A Tribunal awards ₹9,00,000 with 7.5% simple interest from the petition date (1 April 2023) to deposit (31 March 2025). Interest payable is:
e: Two full years: 9,00,000 × 7.5% × 2 = ₹1,35,000 simple interest under s.171.

t: Interest of ₹1,20,000 is payable to a single claimant who has NOT furnished PAN. The TDS to be deducted is:
e: Interest exceeds ₹50,000, so TDS applies; without PAN the rate is 20%: 1,20,000 × 20% = ₹24,000 (10% if PAN furnished).

t: A family receives ₹2,00,000 from the Hit and Run Compensation Fund for a death. The offending vehicle is later identified and the Tribunal assesses compensation at ₹14,00,000 against the insurer. The insurer pays:
o: ₹12,00,000, after adjusting the hit-and-run compensation already received
₹9,00,000 after also deducting ₹5 lakh under Section 164
e: Compensation paid under the hit-and-run scheme/Fund is deductible from any compensation the victim later obtains from the Tribunal for the same accident.

t: An accident occurs in March 2022. The deceased leaves a wife and one child. Applying 10% enhancement per three-year span since October 2017, the conventional heads total:
e: One span (Oct 2017–Oct 2020) completed → +10%: consortium 44,000 × 2 = 88,000, loss of estate 16,500, funeral 16,500 → ₹1,21,000.

t: A 25-year-old permanent employee earning ₹25,000 per month dies leaving a wife only. Loss of dependency is:
e: 3,00,000 + 50% = 4,50,000; wife as sole dependant → married, deduct 1/3 = 3,00,000; × multiplier 18 (21–25) = ₹54,00,000.

t: The Tribunal awards ₹44,000 as compensation plus interest; the insurer disputes the entire amount. The maximum deposit payable with the appeal, if an appeal were maintainable, would be ₹22,000. In fact:
o: Appeal lies to the District Court instead
No appeal lies at all, since the amount in dispute is below ₹1,00,000
e: Irrespective of the deposit arithmetic (lower of ₹25,000 or 50%), s.173(2) bars appeals where the amount in dispute is less than one lakh rupees.
